items.d: 중국의 여성 스파이 앨리스 황이 대만계인 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)와 ‘긴밀한(close)’ 관계를 맺고 정보를 수집해 온 것으로 미국 정보 당국이 판단했다고 29일(현지 시간) 뉴욕타임스(NYT)가 보도했다. 중국 정부와 엔비디아는 모두 보도 내용을 부인했다. 미국 정보 당국은 2024년 싱가포르에 본사를 둔 데이터센터 회사 메가스피드 임원인 앨리스 황을 조사하는 과정에서 그가 황 CEO와 접촉하고 있다는 점을 파악했다. 당국은 메가스피드가 중국 수출이 금지된 엔비디아의 첨단 인공지능(AI) 칩을 중국으로 우회 공급할 가능성을 의심한 것으로 알려졌다. 소셜미디어 링크트인에는 황 CEO가 2024년 대만 타이베이의 술집에서 앨리스 황의 옆자리에서 술을 마시는 사진이 있다. NYT에 따르면 도널드

items.t: New report says Nvidia CEO was possible target of Chinese spy plot
items.d: A new report from the New York Times reveals that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a possible Chinese spy plot, involving an executive at a Singapore-based company. NBC News has not independently confirmed the details of the investigation.

items.fullText: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future Jensen Huang’s visit to the nation’s capital, Astana — including a presidential meeting and public fireside chat — coincided with new AI infrastructure commitments anchored by NVIDIA compute. October 22, 2026 by Rev Lebaredian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity.
